title: dedicated-autoscaler-tokenbucket-smoothing-throughput-guarantees-fix-v2
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: Dedicated autoscaler token-bucket smoothing was introduced to prevent short-lived request bursts from permanently inflating provisioned throughput. We observed a regression in canaries where smoothing double-counted transient refill events when a node rejoined a pool, causing sustained over-provisioning and violations of throughput guarantees for smaller fleets. Motivation: fix the tokenbucket smoothing math so transient bump events are correctly attenuated, add observability to detect regressions, and harden the rollout plan. This PR contains a targeted bugfix, tests, and monitoring additions. Changes: 1) Fix smoothing window state: ensure per-node refill events are deduplicated by node_id and timestamp window to prevent double-accumulation on rapid requeues. 2) Adjust token replenish logic to clamp replenishment to configured max_burst tokens per smoothing interval. 3) Introduce two new metrics: dedicated_autoscaler.burst_utilization and dedicated_autoscaler.smoothing_latency. 4) Add integration tests simulating node churn and transient high-qps spikes. 5) Small docs update for dedicated autoscaler config defaults and rollout guidance. Testing and CI: unit tests updated and expanded; integration tests added to the autoscaler test-suite. CI flaked once on an unrelated infra test and was re-run; final CI status: pass. Rollout: canary to 10% of Dedicated fleets for 24h, monitor burst_utilization, queueing_time, and per-fleet cost delta. Related: ENG-3482 (autoscaler stability), SUP-502 (customer report on over-provisioning).
commits: fix(autoscaler): dedupe tokenbucket refill events by node_id and window
fix(autoscaler): clamp replenish amount to max_burst per smoothing interval
test(autoscaler): add churn + transient-burst integration test (node rejoin)
docs(dedicated): document smoothing defaults and canary checklist

María Gómez: Metrics names are fine. Please ensure smoothing_latency is exposed with histogram buckets matching other autoscaler histograms.
Aisha Patel: Updated metrics to use existing autoscaler histogram buckets to keep dashboards consistent.
Omar Hassan: Integration test reproduced the regressions locally and the fix resolves the over-provisioning signal. Approving pending CI pass.
ci_checks: integration-tests: pass (re-run after flaky infra test)
release_notes: Fix tokenbucket smoothing double-counting bug in Dedicated autoscaler which could cause over-provisioning during node churn. Adds new metrics (burst_utilization, smoothing_latency) and improves default smoothing semantics.
rollout: Canary to 10% of Dedicated fleets for 24h with automated rollback if burst_utilization or queueing_time exceed thresholds for more than 5 minutes.
risk_assessment: low-medium: change is localized to autoscaler smoothing logic and covered by unit and integration tests. Canary rollout mitigates risk.
